Pain During Intimacy Deserves a Cause-Focused Assessment

Pain during sexual activity or penetration can have many causes, including dryness, tissue irritation, pelvic-floor factors, scarring, infection or other gynaecological conditions. It should not automatically be treated as a cosmetic problem. NeoSculpt6 provides a confidential assessment to understand the symptom pattern and identify whether gynaecological, pelvic-floor, medical or selected procedural care is appropriate.

What Is Pain During Intimacy?

Pain during intimacy, often described clinically as dyspareunia, refers to recurrent or persistent pain associated with penetration or sexual activity. The pain may occur at the vaginal opening, within the vagina or deeper in the pelvis.

Possible causes vary and can include dryness, hormonal change, irritation, infection, scar tissue, pelvic-floor dysfunction or other gynaecological conditions. Treatment should therefore target the identified cause rather than the symptom label alone.

Understand When, Where and Why the Pain Occurs

The consultation reviews when pain started, whether it is superficial or deeper, dryness, menstrual or menopause context, childbirth or surgical history, medication use, infection symptoms and previous treatment. Examination, testing or referral is recommended only when clinically indicated.

OUR PROCESS

Treatment Process

The symptom pattern, timing, triggers, relevant medical history and previous treatment are discussed in a private setting.

Hormonal, pelvic-floor, urinary, medication, irritation, infection or other relevant factors are considered according to the concern.

Examination, testing or referral is recommended only when clinically indicated and with appropriate consent.

Supportive care, medical evaluation, rehabilitation or a selected procedure is discussed according to the likely cause rather than the symptom label alone.

Symptom response is reviewed and persistent, worsening or unexplained concerns are reassessed or referred appropriately.

Who Can Benefit

  • Persistent Pain with Penetration

    Patients with recurrent discomfort who want a clinical assessment.

  • Postpartum or Scar-Related Pain

    Patients whose symptoms began after childbirth, tearing, episiotomy or surgery.

  • Dryness-Associated Discomfort

    Patients whose pain occurs with reduced lubrication or irritation.

  • Unexplained Recurrent Pain

    Patients who need evaluation for gynaecological, pelvic-floor or other contributing factors.

Sudden severe pain, bleeding, fever, significant discharge or other concerning symptoms may require prompt medical evaluation.
